verdict.rationale: Highnote's spend rules and velocity controls let users define rules on MCC, amount, authorization count and time windows. Those rules are evaluated automatically on every authorization event and permit or restrict the transaction. That is real rule-to-action automation, but it is limited to approve/decline decisions on authorizations. Webhook notifications only deliver events outward and are not rule-triggered actions. Missing for 10: a general event-to-action rules engine covering events beyond authorizations, configurable action types beyond permit/decline, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Spend rules let you automate logic on authorizations that permit or restrict transactions. You can configure that logic on merchant category codes (MCC), dollar amount, authorization count, and more.
Every rule is evaluated at authorization, before funds move.
Velocity controls allow time boundary constraints to be applied to a spend rule.
Set rules once at the program level and they apply uniformly across every card.
